Job Description And Duties
Join Our Team!

CDSS is looking for a highly motivated Research Data Analyst I/II (RDA I/II) with strong math, analytical skills and experience to join the Fiscal Forecasting Branch (FFB). The FFB is comprised of three bureaus: Family Engagement and Equity Estimates Bureau (FEEEB), Children, Adult, and Housing Programs Estimates Bureau (CAHPEB), and the Child Care Fiscal Services Bureau. The FFB develops the annual Local Assistance Governor’s Budget and May Revision update for programs administered by the County Welfare Departments. In addition, the FFB is responsible in providing a fiscal analysis of proposed legislative bills that have a potential impact to the Department.

The RDA II’s are senior analysts that work with minimal direction. It is essential for the RDA I/II to possess a strong background in mathematics and statistics as well as analytical skills to conceptualize, develop, and create fiscal estimates that are robust and consider multiple variables (e.g., funding environment, political considerations, data integration). The work intersects with multiple branches across the department and the RDA I/II needs to develop strong working relationships to be successful. The work produced will be scrutinized closely by senior management, executive staff, and external stakeholders because it will have direct implications for the State Budget.

It is desirable that the RDA I/II have an understanding of social service programs’ policies and experience in interpreting and applying statutes, regulations and procedures. Additionally, the RDA I/II must be able to work independently, reason logically, and possess strong analytical skills. The RDA I/II is expected to mentor junior staff members, take a lead role in complex assignments, and work as an acting manager when required. For this RDA I/II position, it is essential the applicant has a strong research background from academia and/or from work experience in a data driven environment.

About Second Harvest Of Silicon Valley

Founded in 1974, Second Harvest of Silicon Valley is one of the largest food banks in the nation and a trusted nonprofit leader in ending local hunger. The organization distributes nutritious groceries through a network of nearly 400 partners at drive-thru and walk-up sites across Santa Clara and San Mateo counties. Due to the prohibitively expensive cost of living in Silicon Valley, the economic downturn caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the rise in inflation, Second Harvest is now serving an average of about 500,000 people every month. Second Harvest also connects people to federal nutrition programs and other food resources, and advocates for anti- hunger policies on the local, state and national levels. To learn more about how Second Harvest is responding to the incredible amount of need in Silicon Valley, visit shfb.org.

About The Position

The main responsibilities of this role include supporting Second Harvest free grocery distribution

programs across multiple regions, forming deep community relationships, and helping ensure effective, compliant, and client-centered food distributions. Program Coordinators support a portfolio of at least four regions by working closely with Regional Program Managers to deliver consistent, best-in-class client and volunteer experience. The Regional Program Manager for Program Coordinators will provide leadership and guidance to Program Coordinators, helping them prioritize responsibilities, manage their time effectively, and maximize their impact across the regions they support. Coordinators focus on free grocery program site support, community engagement, supply bins & special projects, and volunteer experience. This position dedicates 50-60% of the time to working actively in the community, supporting food distribution programs, engaging volunteers, and building community relationships, while the remaining time is spent on administrative responsibilities and internal coordination to ensure seamless distribution operations.

This Job Might Be For You If

You are passionate about ending hunger and building community solutions to ending poverty and food insecurity.
You are a curious learner who can listen deeply and synthesize various perspectives and communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders about what you learn.
You find fulfillment in cultivating and sustaining relationships, demonstrating cultural humility in your interactions with a diverse range of clients, volunteers, representatives from partner organizations, and colleagues.
You enjoy identifying, planning, designing, and implementing programs, changes, and initiatives that enhance the community's well-being, finding satisfaction in meeting its evolving needs.

Founded in 1974, Second Harvest of Silicon Valley is one of the largest food banks in the nation and a trusted nonprofit leader in ending local hunger. Position Description

The Program Coordinator - Social Services
is a position located in the Department of Social Services and is responsible for performing professional duties involved in assisting individuals and customers with overcoming barriers to become self-sufficient and have the best quality of life possible. The incumbent will work with all populations, except for minors, including homeless individuals and families and those at risk of becoming homeless.

Metropolitan Social Services (MSS), a department of Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County, focuses on topics and issues continually effecting the economic and social wellbeing of Nashvillians. National and local policy choices have resulted in a deterioration of standard of living and put more people into poverty. Poverty can be multidimensional and result from long-term processes of inequality, persistent exclusion, concentration of economic power, access to wealth-building and social capital, as well as broad transformations in work and society.

Typical Duties

Assessing eligibility of customers according to established agency policies and procedures.
Providing information and referral services to customers and the public in a courteous and timely manner.
Providing case management services to all populations served.
Making home visits to customers' homes and/or other agencies/locations within the community and/or designated collocated partnership sites.
Providing customers with the information that enables them to utilize the programs' services to best address their needs.
Multi-tasking and working in multiple case management systems and computer applications.
Performing concise, comprehensive social assessments and developing service plans based on the customers' individual needs.
Working with the Public Defender's & Conservatorship partnership as it pertains to the case management, implementation and monitoring of the data/outcomes.
Working with various established Metro partnerships such as the Office of Conservatorship Management, and the HERO'S program through Metro Nashville Public Schools.
Completing a detailed Social comprehensive assessment and all needed documentation and forms completely, accurately and in a timely and ongoing manner.
Building working relationships with various Metro Departments and other agencies to ensure the emotional and social well-being of the assigned constituents are being met, assessed and documented on a regular basis.
Facilitating program specific groups.
Attending meetings and trainings as needed.
Placing all data in the case management system accurately and in a timely manner.
Participating in MSS sponsored events as well as representing the agency at other community events.
Responsible for all weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual reports.
Assumes other duties as needed and/or assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, and (2) two years of experience in program administration.

Licenses Required

Valid Driver License

Candidates with accreditations earned in a foreign institute are encouraged to apply.

Professional social work or case management experience in the mental health, domestic violence, homelessness and/or substance abuse field
Skilled in interviewing, making case assessment, counseling and assisting clients in goal formulation and realizations and case referrals
Experience with conservatorship programs and issues
Bilingual

Job Summary

This position will support two NIH-funded grants focused on the development and dissemination of the NIH Baby Toolbox. Responsibilities include assessing infant and toddler participants, conducting interviews with parents and researchers, assisting with the implementation of new research protocols, supporting the logistics and materials for training workshops, providing assistance to workshop attendees, and helping develop content for an online training platform.

Opportunities for co-authorship on scientific publications and conference presentations are available. Applicants should have an interest in working with young children, collaborating as part of a research team, and be willing to work in person three days per week in downtown Chicago. Occasional evening and weekend availability may be required.

Specific Responsibilities

Technical

Leads execution & control of a biomedical &/or social science project or research study.
Ensures completion of study activities per protocol including recruitment.
Ascertains pretreatment & eligibility requirements.
Obtains informed consent.
Registers participant with appropriate sponsor.
Interviews & obtains medical & social histories.
Administers, schedules &/or scores tests.

Administration

Oversees & manages collection, maintenance, analysis & evaluation of data that will be used in grant submissions, presentations & publications.
Ensures that information is entered correctly into databases.
Assists PI in reviewing, analyzing, interpreting, summarizing, formatting, editing, & preparing tables, charts, graphs, progress & final reports, etc.

Finance

Orders & maintains inventory of study supplies.

Supervision

Trains, directs, assigns duties to & supervises research staff, students, residents &/or fellows.
Acts as a mentor in regard to education of junior coordinators.

Miscellaneous

Perform other duties as assigned

Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree in a major such as social or health science or related; OR appropriate combination of education and experience and 3 years' research study or other relevant experience required; OR
Successful completion of a full course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a master's or higher degree in a major such as social or health science or related; OR appropriate combination of education and experience and 1 year research study or other relevant experience.
Supervisory or project management experience required.
Must complete NU's IRB CITI training before interacting with any participants & must re-certify every 3 years.

Experience with standardized assessments including the NIH Baby Toolbox or similar assessment platforms (e.g., Mullen, Bayley)
Experience testing children ages 0-3 years
Experience working in a developmental research laboratory
Degree in Psychology, Child Development, or a related field
